title: Sales Development Representative
description:
Sales Development Representative | Remote * | $22.50/hr. base + uncapped commission

Construction contractors on government projects must prove they paid prevailing wage, every week, on every job. If they get it wrong, they risk penalties, fees, and lost contracts. eBacon 's software makes the process simple. Your job is to find the contractors who need us and book meetings for our regional account executives.

What you'll do

• Work your own dedicated database of construction contractors in HubSpot, calling and emailing to identify leads and set meetings.

• Schedule qualified appointments to AEs covering multiple states, targeting ten meetings per week.

• Learn how to talk about certified payroll and Davis-Bacon compliance from us. No construction background is needed.

What you'll earn

• $22.50/hr base ($46K) plus uncapped commission, paid semi-monthly. First-year reps typically earn $6K to $12K in comission, and our top producer earned $24K in commission last year.

• Up to 6% 401(k) match, 15 days PTO, and a benefits allowance for medical, dental, vision, and life.

• Every Friday ends at 2:30pm!

What we're looking for

• 1+ year of outbound phone sales or other high-volume phone work.

• Comfort with 100+ calls a day and hearing "no" without taking it personally.

• Clear, confident writing for follow-up emails.

• HubSpot or B2B SaaS experience is a plus.

Schedule: Mon to Thu 8am to 5pm, Fri 8am to 2:30pm, Arizona time (no daylight saving). This is a strong fit for candidates in Mountain or Central time.

Who we are
eBacon is a financial technology company in Phoenix, Arizona, focused on certified payroll and fringe benefit management for the construction industry. Our development team is in-house, and we've won awards for customer service and for being one of Arizona's top places to work, several years running. Several of our reps have been with us 8 to 10 years. The work is serious, but we don't take ourselves too seriously. We do have a bacon strip mascot.

*Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future sponsorship. Background screening required.

title: SDK Engineer - Python
description:
ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a SDK Engineer - Python to join our SDK team and own how developers talk to Supabase from Python. You'll work closely with the rest of the SDK team, our Auth, Realtime, Storage, PostgREST, Functions, CLI and Docs teams, and the open-source community, helping us make the Python SDK a library Python developers genuinely enjoy using.

Python developers reach Supabase from backend services, data pipelines, notebooks, and a growing number of AI agents and agent frameworks. The Python SDK is how all of them talk to the platform: database queries, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions, in both sync and async flavors.

This is a library-authoring role, and the work happens in the open: public repos, public issue trackers, and API decisions whose consequences last for years. If you get satisfaction from a type checker that catches the bug before your users do, from an async client that cleans up after itself, and from an issue tracker that isn't a graveyard, you'll like it here.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

- Build and evolve our Python SDK across database, auth, storage, realtime and functions, with both sync and async APIs that feel natural in Python.

- Start new things. Alongside the maintenance work, find what's missing, make the case for it, and build it. Nobody will hand you the list.

- Work in the open. Triage inbound issues, review and shepherd outside contributions, keep CI and release automation healthy, and hold a clear, kind line on scope.

- Own the typing experience. Make the SDK fully typed and checker-friendly, so autocomplete and static analysis stay correct in real codebases.

- Keep us honest across environments. Multiple Python versions, sync and async frameworks, workers, serverless and notebooks - with dependency ranges that don't fight our users' projects. Test it, don't assume it.

- Work on realtime. Long-lived websocket connections, reconnection, and subscription and presence semantics.

- Track the platform. When auth, realtime, storage, postgrest or edge functions ship a change, make sure the SDK reflects it, and that we say so in the changelog.

- Design in public. Write the RFCs, migration guides, release notes and docs. Treat a breaking change as a deprecation path plus a migration story, not a version bump.

- Make our SDK legible to AI coding agents, which are now a major consumer of it.

YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

- Know modern Python typing deeply. You use generics, protocols, overloads and TypedDict as design tools, run strict type checking, and fix type errors without reaching for Any.

- Have authored or maintained a published library with a public API and users outside your own company. You know what it costs to change something people depend on.

- Know the maintainer side of open source. Issue triage at volume, reviewing outside PRs, release automation, changelogs and semver, security reports, and saying no to a feature request without losing the person who asked.

- Are fluent in asyncio and have opinions on how a library should serve both sync and async callers.

- Know Python packaging for libraries: pyproject.toml, wheels, modern tooling, version support policy, and why libraries shouldn't pin their dependencies tightly.

- Test as a habit: unit, type-level and end-to-end against a real stack. Every fix comes with a regression test.

- Write well. Design docs, changelogs and issue replies are a large part of the output here, much of it public, and we're async by default.

title: Analytics Engineer, Finance and Modeling
description:
At In Tandem , we build technology that helps families manage everyday routines and navigate life’s biggest transitions. Through our four brands-OurFamilyWizard, Cozi, FamilyWall, and Custody Navigator-we help families stay organized, communicate well, and foster healthy childhoods. We believe technology should strengthen relationships and make daily coordination less complicated. Everything we create is designed to lighten the mental load, reduce conflict, and support families through big and small moments. If you want your work to make a real difference in the daily lives of parents and kids, In Tandem is the place where your impact will truly matter.

As an Analytics Engineer (Finance & Modeling) , you'll own the metrics, reporting and reconciliation our financial decisions rest on, turning subscription and transaction data across OurFamilyWizard, Cozi, FamilyWall and Custody Navigator into numbers the business can defend. As that foundation becomes automatic, the work shifts toward forecasting and modeling.

You won't start from scratch. Our dbt project is live on Databricks with a star-schema finance mart in production and documented in Unity Catalog. What's missing is the layer on top, and that layer is yours. We also run an internal AI agent that answers business questions in Slack off the semantic layer, so every metric you define and test becomes a question Finance can ask directly rather than queue.

What you'll accomplish:

•
Governed metrics. Add the definitions the finance mart doesn't have yet (ARR, renewal rate, churn, CAC), versioned in dbt and documented in Unity Catalog, with the tests that make each one defensible, and wired into the agent so Finance can ask them directly.

•
Reporting Finance can run without you. Move the recurring finance pack into marimo, retire the Tableau views behind it, and turn a monthly hand-build into something that runs on a schedule.

•
Numbers that reconcile. Reconcile transactions across the app stores, payment processors, subscription systems and the ledger, with automated checks that alert rather than surface at close. Route discrepancies upstream with the evidence attached and turn each one into a test. You build the checks and escalate. Accounting owns the treatment.

•
Forecasting for Finance. Cohort subscriber and revenue projection, and aggregate renewal and retention forecasting, feeding the CFO's forecast and board reporting. LTV by acquisition source, feeding paid spend allocation with Growth. Pricing and promo impact, modeled before we ship rather than measured after. Individual churn propensity and uplift follow once there's a retention motion ready to act on the scores.

• Models ship as scored tables in dbt and Unity Catalog, with tests, lineage and a definition the agent can answer from. Not as notebooks.

Who you are:

• Statistically rigorous. You know why a cohort curve is the wrong shape, what a model is leaking, and when a result is noise.

• Fluent in finance, and unwilling to let a number you can't explain go out the door. When two systems disagree, you find out why and tell the people upstream.

• An engineer who owns the number end to end, from a CFO's question through the model, the test, the report and the conversation that follows. A spreadsheet nobody can reproduce reads to you as a liability.

• AI-proficient in practice, not in theory. Claude Code, coding agents and agent SDKs are part of our daily loop, and we expect you to already work this way. A lot of what used to be a week of modeling work is now an afternoon, and we're hiring for people who have internalized that.

• Willing to wear several hats. This is a small team supporting four brands. Some weeks you're deep in a retention model, some weeks you're chasing an app store discrepancy or unblocking someone else's dashboard. The scope above is the center of the role, not a fence around it.

• Motivated by work that matters. Families rely on these products during real moments in their lives.

description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne , c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable . Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain .
Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.
L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !
Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.
Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.
🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

En tant que post-doctorant.e, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affectées au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS). Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal, « en décortiquant » la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.
Grâce à des outils d’élaboration et de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nous déployons le concept de «Material by design» : concevoir au mieux les matériaux de demain répondant aux enjeux de transition.
Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

Ce post-doctorat s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet VARIMA (VAlorisation des Résidus d’Incinération en Matériaux Avancés) du dispositif Partenariats d'innovation Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes - volet Preuves de Concept. L’incinération des déchets ménagers produit, en plus de l'énergie, des résidus contenant des métaux et des minéraux. Des entreprises récupèrent et recyclent les différents métaux. Cependant, des milliers de tonnes de poussières minérales sont générées et sont généralement envoyées en décharge faute de solution de valorisation.
Ce post-doctorat, d’une durée de 18 mois vise à étudier la valorisation des poussières d’incinération par deux voies d’élaboration : voie géopolymères et voie métallurgie des poudres. Les matériaux obtenus seront ensuite caractérisés au niveau microstructural mais aussi au niveau des propriétés d’usage (propriétés mécanique et thermique ainsi que la tenue à la lixiviation). Le post-doctorant.e contribuera durant la deuxième année de ce CDD à une étude d’impact relative au procédés développés.
· Vous faites preuve d'une grande autonomie dans la conduite de vos travaux expérimentaux tout en montrant une rigueur scientifique exemplaire
· Vous rendez compte des résultats à vos encadrants et à l’entreprise partenaire du projet
· Vous participez aux réunions de suivi de projet et à la rédaction des livrable

title: Equity Research AI Research Contributor
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Aptura is looking for Subject Matter Experts from sell-side or buy-side equity research, covering any sector, who build initiating coverage models, earnings models and data packs in Excel. You have used AI tools on your own work and been frustrated by the mistakes they make. You will turn that experience into realistic Excel tasks that test how well AI does the modelling work of a Research Associate.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Writing realistic Excel tasks drawn from your own work: extending existing models, fixing broken ones and building from a brief

- Working through each task yourself so there is a clear, correct answer

- Writing yes-or-no criteria precise enough that a grader can mark any attempt against them

NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS

- 3+ years in sell-side or buy-side equity research, covering a defined sector or universe of stocks (e.g. TMT, Healthcare, Financials, Energy, Consumer, Industrials)

- Deep hands-on Excel: earnings extraction and prediction, calendarisation, SOTP valuation, data packs and nested formulas

- Strong written English communication skills.

- Attention to detail, and willingness to learn concepts in AI and Evals

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

- Start Date : Immediate

- Duration: Approximately 4-6 weeks

- Payment: task-based. Experts who complete their first task within the required timeline will then be qualified to do multiple tasks for the remainder of the project.

CONTRACT AND PAYMENT TERMS

- You will be engaged as an independent contractor.

- This is a fully remote role that can be completed on your own schedule.

- Projects can be extended, shortened, or concluded early depending on needs and performance.

- Your work at Aptura will not involve access to confidential or proprietary information from any employer, client, or institution.

- Payments will be weekly following task completion.

GETTING STARTED

- Apply with your details and CV. Choose an available 30-minute group walkthrough call.

- Attend the walkthrough and create one original task from your own work. Submit the brief, the actual input workbook(s) needed to complete it. Input-file uploads are compulsory.

- Write the brief yourself. Input workbooks must also be human-built. Use real data that has been sanitised, or public data with the source named. No AI usage allowed.

- We run your task against current frontier AI models. If the models get it wrong, you then write a detailed yes-or-no rubric, and a reviewer signs off on the task with you.

- Completing onboarding does not guarantee a job offer; selection remains subject to written approval of the task proposal.

ABOUT APTURA

Aptura is an applied AI and data company working with frontier labs to train AI systems on real professional work. We do this by building high-quality evaluation and training environments that teach AI agents to produce work that can be used in daily workflows.

Our client is a frontier data research lab. Their thesis: models are what they eat. A large share of training compute is burned on data that's redundant, irrelevant, or harmful - so they built a platform that automatically curates petabytes of raw data into high-quality training data. It's modality-agnostic, needs no labels, and runs inside the customer's own cloud or on-prem.
The results are concrete: 7-40x faster training, performance as if trained on 10x+ more raw data, and models with less than half the parameters beating larger ones. AI labs and enterprises use it to train and adapt their own models.
Our client has raised ~$60M across Seed and Series A, led by Felicis and Amplify Partners, with Radical Ventures, Microsoft, and Amazon. Angels include Geoff Hinton, Yann LeCun, and Jeff Dean. The team is growing fast on the back of a strong enterprise pipeline.

Every company should own its intelligence. Our client wants every AI team - not just the frontier labs - to have frontier-quality training data and full control over the cost and roadmap of their own models.

Based in Bristol, UK, you’ll develop board and PCBA hardware tests that help turn complex designs into reliable products. You’ll take tests from initial design analysis to deployment, then support them in factories and the field.

title: Lead Data Scientist, AdTech
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato .

YOUR ROLE
You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.
Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.
We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.
By the end of your first year:

• Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier

• Carrier conversion data running in production models

• Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale

• A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions

• Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives

• Output the business trusts and uses without rework

MUST HAVE

• 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact

• Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.

• You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included

• You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift

• You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view

• Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

• Real ad budget spent in live auctions

• Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems

• Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms

• Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration

• Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior

• AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker

• CI/CD deployment

title: Cloud Architect Internship
description:
Overview: Multi-Tenant Cloud Infrastructure Design
The Cloud Architect is responsible for designing, managing, and optimizing the entire multi-tenant cloud infrastructure that hosts our integrated supply chain e-commerce platform. While our current stack utilizes Oracle Cloud Free VMs, this role requires expertise in major public clouds (AWS/GCP/Azure) to architect scalable, resilient, cost-optimized, and compliant solutions that handle fluctuating e-commerce traffic, stable internal tool usage, and intensive AI agent compute demands.
Internship Details
Duration: 3 months
Start Date: Immediate
Location: Remote
Stipend: None initially. Based on your first-quarter performance, you may be offered a paid full-time opportunity, or even be absorbed directly by the client as an FTE.
Key Responsibilities & Core Projects
You will design and govern the platform's foundation, ensuring scalability and compliance across all environments.

• Cloud Architecture Design: Design and evolve the target cloud infrastructure (utilizing AWS, GCP, or Azure best practices) for maximum scalability, security, and high-availability, ensuring the platform can reliably support the MES $\rightarrow$ WMS $\rightarrow$ OMS flow.

• Capacity Planning & Optimization: Plan and optimize resource allocation to effectively handle unpredictable e-commerce traffic spikes and the specific compute requirements for AI agent training and inference, driving cost efficiency.

• High Availability & Disaster Recovery (DR): Implement multi-region/multi-AZ high-availability architectures and define comprehensive Disaster Recovery (DR) strategies for all core services, including PostgreSQL 15 and Redis.

• Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) Governance: Establish and enforce best practices for Terraform usage, ensuring configuration consistency, security compliance, and auditable infrastructure changes.

• Security & Compliance: Conduct regular security reviews of cloud configurations (e.g., IAM, VPC/VNet, Storage) and ensure architecture aligns with data residency and compliance requirements relevant to our multi-tenant operations.

• Service Integration: Architect the network and service mesh overlay that integrates the containerized applications (Docker/Traefik) with external cloud services and the overall monitoring solution (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry).

Required Technologies & Tools
Candidates must possess deep architectural experience with public cloud providers and infrastructure automation:

• Cloud Providers: Expert-level proficiency in at least one major public cloud (AWS, GCP, or Azure).

• Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC): Mandatory expertise in Terraform for cloud resource provisioning.

• Containerization: Deep knowledge of Docker networking, security, and orchestration principles.

• Networking & Edge: Experience configuring load balancing, service mesh, and ingress controllers (e.g., Traefik).

• Data & Storage: Architecting scalable database services (PostgreSQL) and object storage (MinIO).

• Security: Cloud security best practices, IAM policy design, and network segmentation.

AI Agent Focus
You will optimize the cloud layer for our emerging AI capabilities.

• Compute Optimization: Design elastic and cost-effective compute clusters (e.g., GPU instances) to efficiently handle the variable demands of LLM fine-tuning and multi-agent system orchestration.

• Data Residency: Architect the data pipeline and storage solutions to ensure that training data and model artifacts adhere to strict data residency requirements across tenants.

Success Metrics & Career Path
Performance will be measured by:

• Cost Efficiency: Demonstrable reduction in cloud operational costs (FinOps) while maintaining performance.

• Availability: Achieving defined SLAs/SLOs for infrastructure uptime and performance.

• Compliance: Successful implementation and auditing of cloud security and data residency controls.

WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

TEAM AND ROLE

- Shape the architecture of the world’s first commercial fusion power plant - Own system-level decisions that determine how a first-of-a-kind energy technology is designed, integrated, and ultimately deployed at scale.

- Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in industry - Work across tightly coupled disciplines (plasma physics, magnets, cryogenics, manufacturing, controls, and more) to resolve critical trade-offs and turn cutting-edge science into a functioning product.

- Build real hardware with a pragmatic, fast-moving team from all over the world - Combine advanced simulation and systems thinking with a strong execution mindset, focusing on practical engineering solutions that accelerate the path to commercial fusion energy.

 

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

- You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

- You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

- Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

- Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

 

YOUR IMPACT

As a Senior Computational Physicist - Stellarator Optimization, you will design the magnetic fields and coils at the core of our stellarators. You will balance plasma performance with engineering requirements, prioritizing simple, practical designs that can be built. Your work will directly shape Stellaris, our first commercial fusion power plant.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

You will shape the “heart” of the stellarator: the magnetic field that confines the plasma and the coils that create it.

- Release optimized plasma and coil geometries that engineering teams use to design magnets, supporting structures, and surrounding sub-systems.

- Resolve design trade-offs between physics, engineering and assembly requirements.

- Own research projects that overcome technical challenges. Choose questions by their impact to the stellarator and carry the answers through to engineering decisions.

- Deliver results in time for design milestones, with clear recommendations, checked assumptions, and uncertainties that engineers can work with.

For companies building financial technology and transforming the financial services space, the biggest bottleneck to their growth and innovation is often the underlying banks and infrastructure stack they rely on. We have spent our careers founding and scaling companies like Plaid, Square, Meta, Blend, and Affirm, and have seen this problem firsthand - builders and developers needing to partner with traditional banks, and creating API and abstraction layers over the patchwork that is the bank, its core, and many other vendors. All of this results in a complex (and often expensive) banking supply chain involving a user, fintech, BaaS middleware provider, bank, core and the Federal Reserve.

At Column, we set out to simplify and fix this. We are a bank and a software company built from the ground up, offering builders and developers technology-forward banking solutions that cut out the hundreds of vendors, middleware providers, and abstraction layers. This means a safer, more transparent, and less costly banking supply chain. Come build with us!

THE OPPORTUNITY:

Column's Compliance team plays a critical role in ensuring the Bank grows safely. As a Compliance Analyst, you will be responsible for supporting the Compliance Testing function, leveraging regulatory compliance expertise to ensure our fintech partners’ programs are compliant and sustainable and meet the Bank’s expectations. This is a cross-functional role, working with both first- and second-line colleagues and interfacing directly with our fintech partners. This means exposure to a range of products, business models, and regulatory questions you won’t find at a traditional bank. This role is a great opportunity for someone who is passionate about regulatory compliance and wants hands-on experience testing a wide variety of fintech products, partners, and business models to accelerate their compliance career.

This role is a fixed-term contract, remote position with an initial contract duration of six months and the potential to extend based on performance.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Conduct compliance testing, both across Column’s products and services and at the Bank’s partners, as a contributor to Column’s Compliance Testing & Monitoring Program

- Clearly document assessment findings, and own the drafting and reporting of results derived from the Compliance Testing Program

- Identify potential areas of weakness (inadequate/ineffective controls, areas of non-compliance, etc.) within the Bank, and work with partners to strengthen the associated control environment

- Monitor, interpret, and assess potential regulatory changes that may impact the Bank. Work with business, risk, and legal partners to ensure new regulatory requirements are clearly understood and processes are in place before their effective dates

WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL:

- Bachelor’s degree and/or equivalent experience

- 3+ years in compliance or audit; experience at a regulated financial institution is a plus

- Detail-oriented with excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills

- Experience navigating banking regulations and applying rules to the Bank’s products

- Demonstrated project management skills and the ability to juggle execution across multiple stakeholders

- Certified Regulatory Compliance Manager (CRCM), Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS), or equivalent certification a plus

- Curiosity, eagerness to learn, and excitement about regulatory compliance and partner banking

WHAT YOU'LL GET FROM US:

- 🏥 Comprehensive health, dental, and vision plans, including options that are 100% covered by Column for you

- 💳 FSA and HSA account options to enable use of pre-tax money for medical and dependent care expenses

- 🌴 Paid PTO, including 15 days of vacation and 10 days of sick leave each year

- 📈 Eligibility to participate in Column’s 401k plan, including self-directed brokerage options

title: Founding Engineer (m/w/d)
description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

Tax advisory runs on structured data, recurring work and clear rules, and almost none of it has been rebuilt with modern software. What decides who gets there first is real case data and engineers who build next to the people doing the work.

Vogel advises several thousand mid-sized companies and acquires established advisory firms, developing them further on one shared base. On top of the systems we buy, we build our own software: a data layer above DATEV, the tools our advisors use every day, and agents that take over recurring work. What counts is daily use, on data that is audited and closed.

As one of our first engineers, you build across the whole stack: data pipelines, backend, the interfaces advisors use and the agents on top. You take a problem from the first conversation with an advisor to software that runs every day. We are hiring our CTO in parallel, who will own the architecture and lead the team. You work directly with Moritz Vogel.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Tools advisors use

- Sit with tax advisors and accountants on real cases, find where the work gets stuck, and turn it into software they use the next day. Your benchmark: an advisor would miss it if it were switched off.

- Build interfaces, dashboards and internal tools, from the first prototype to something that runs without you.

- Ship small and often: a tool in daily use beats a perfect plan.

Data and integration

- Build the pipelines that move data out of DATEV and our other systems into our own data layer every night, checked from the first day.

- Define every figure exactly once, so a number means the same thing in every tool and report.

- Connect the systems each acquired firm brings, so one more firm never means one more integration project.

Agents and automation

- Build agents that take over recurring work, with a clear line between what the model judges and what is calculated deterministically.

- Make every result traceable by version, source and decision, so a certified professional can sign off on it.

- Evaluate against closed, audited cases, not against test data.

QUESTIONS YOU'LL ANSWER

- Which recurring task in an accounting team is the first one worth taking off people's hands, and how do you prove it?

- How do you build fast now without leaving a mess for the next engineer?

- When is a prototype ready to run on real data every day, and who signs off before it does?

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

- 3 months: Your first tool is in daily use by an advisory team, and the nightly data load runs with checks.

- 6 months: Several tools and the first agents run in regular operation. You own one area end to end, and others build on your code.

- 12 months: You own a part of our software with its own users, and new engineers learn from your standards.

Where it leads: from engineer to owning a product area, as a senior engineer or by leading a team, decided by contribution, not by years served.

WHAT YOU BRING

- A degree in computer science, mathematics, physics, engineering or a related field from a strong university such as TUM, or an equally strong record of your own projects.

- You have shipped software that other people used, at work, as a working student or in your own project.

- You write production code in at least one language, ideally Python or TypeScript, and you are at home with SQL and relational databases.

- AI is your everyday tool: you write, review and test code with it, and you know where it goes wrong.

- You want breadth across data, backend, interface and agents, and you work in German and in person, because our advisors and clients do.

- You learn from practitioners, and you set the highest standard in everything you ship, not because someone checks, but because mediocrity bothers you.

A PLUS, NOT A REQUIREMENT

- One to two years as an engineer in a young startup or scale-up, or a working-student role where you owned something real.

- Knowledge of accounting, tax or DATEV, or data pipelines and agents y

Entity is building the destination for high calibre games on the web. A curated catalogue of bestselling full-scale game titles running natively in the browser: click a link and you’re playing in seconds on the device you already own.
There are no downloads, no installs and no new hardware. This new low-friction way of playing games is powered by the latest developments in web technologies such as WebAssembly and WebGPU, allowing us to render high-quality game experiences on your device. This is not a game streaming service; this is the power of the New Web.
For developers, we’re the official, licensed channel for proper games on the web. We offer self-serve tools to publish, operate and grow their games, with social play, identity and a unique end-to-end business analytics suite built into the platform.

We're hiring a Product Manager to own how that product performs once it's in players' hands. That means how players find games, decide to buy, keep coming back, and what we learn from it every week.

You'll also be close to how players discover and buy games today, and keen to build for where the industry is heading.

• Player funnel. Own the path from waitlist to first session, trial, purchase and return visits. Design and run A/B tests, and turn the results into product changes.

• Live ops. Own the live ops calendar: events, promotions and feature beats. Line it up with the Head of Games' release schedule and marketing's campaigns.

• Product performance. Define the product KPIs, own the dashboards and run a weekly performance review. Turn what you learn into roadmap priorities.

• Early access. Run the early access programme's feedback loop: collect player feedback, sort issues and feed them into the backlog.

title: Software Engineer, Pretraining Data
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, PRETRAINING DATA

We're looking for Software Engineers to build the data systems behind our frontier models' initial training. You'll work on large-scale crawling, data platform, and pipeline infrastructure, turning raw dumps into the datasets our models train on, and making iteration with researchers fast and reliable.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Data Platform:

- Build the platform that turns raw web, code, multimodal, and acquired data into training-ready datasets for frontier pretraining runs

- Own the pipelines, orchestration, and tooling that make pretraining data iteration fast, reliable, observable, and reproducible at scale

- Create clear signals for data quality, lineage, freshness, and pipeline health so researchers can trust what goes into each run

- Partner with initial training, crawling, data quality, and acquisition teams to turn new data ideas into measurable improvements in loss, evals, and model capability

Data Quality:

- Build and own high-throughput, fully telemetered data pipelines that process frontier-scale data with end-to-end traceability. If something breaks or drifts, your systems will tell us before the training run does

- Train and ship models that classify, rank, filter, clean, and identify data at extreme throughput. These models have to be both accurate and fast enough to sit in the critical path without becoming the bottleneck

- Design and run scaling-ladder experiments on data-mixture, repeatability, and quality depth that turn "this dataset feels good" into hard evidence the training team can trust

- Partner tightly with Data Acquisition to hunt down missing or low-quality sources, and with the training teams to close the loop on what actually moves loss and downstream evals

- Treat data quality as a systems problem and a research problem. You will write performance-critical code one week and design careful experiments the next

Crawling:

- Build and scale the web crawling systems that discover, schedule, fetch, and parse high-quality documents across the open web for initial training

- Improve URL seeding, scoring, and fair host scheduling so crawl capacity lands on the hosts and pages that matter most for model quality

title: Senior Software Engineer - Search & AI
description:
Overview: 

We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to build and run the search systems that connect Guidepoint clients with the right experts. You will join the Search team in Data Engineering and own work end to end: Elasticsearch index design and cluster operations, the inference services behind semantic search, the Python services in front of it all, and the AI features that turn a plain-language question into a ranked list of people.

Our search sits on the critical path of the business. When a client asks for experts, the quality and speed of what comes back decides whether a project starts. This role is for someone who cares about relevance as much as uptime, and who can explain why a result ranked where it did.

This role will be hybrid based in our Toronto office. 

What You'll Do:

Search and indexing

• Design index mappings, analyzers, and tokenizers for expert, company, project, and lead data, including semantic_text and dense_vector fields

• Write and tune queries: bool, function_score, nested, aggregations, kNN, and hybrid retrieval

• Plan and run reindexes, Painless data fixes, and alias cutovers with zero downtime (we recently retired Solr completely)

• Build and maintain ingestion: Logstash JDBC pipelines and incremental change feeds from PostgreSQL and SQL Server, including tuning the source SQL when indexing slows down

Cluster operations and maintenance

• Operate Elastic Cloud deployments on Azure across prod, QA, and dev: sizing, shard allocation, ILM, snapshots, and version upgrades

• Monitor cluster health in Datadog and Kibana; tune heap, circuit breakers, and fetch sizes; diagnose shard and recovery problems with the _cat and _cluster APIs

• Manage access: roles, service API keys and their rotation, least-privilege accounts for every consumer

• Lead incident response for latency spikes, circuit breaker trips, and ingestion failures, then write the RCA and ship the follow-up fixes

• Load test search under realistic traffic before major mapping, query, or capacity changes

Inference and AI services

• Run the inference layer behind semantic search: Elasticsearch inference endpoints, embedding models (ELSER, E5, or hosted models), ML node capacity, and cost

• Build services that turn natural-language requests into structured search queries and filters using LLMs

• Build and harden MCP servers that let AI agents call search as a tool: auth, consistent error contracts, lean payloads

• Benchmark LLMs for accuracy, latency, and cost against fixed query batteries, and pick models on evidence

• Set up offline relevance evaluation (judgment lists, nDCG, recall@k) and run A/B tests online

Python services and APIs

• Build and maintain the Python APIs and workers, running on AKS (Kubernetes), that sit between clients, AI agents, and the search cluster

• Own services in production on AKS behind Azure APIM: tests, CI/CD, Docker images, Kubernetes deployments and scaling, dashboards, and alerts

• Fix findings from security scans and keep secrets out of code and images

• Review code and raise the bar on design, testing, and readability across the team

Across the team

• Turn ambiguous product asks into technical designs and break them into deliverable pieces

• Write design docs and runbooks that others can pick up without you in the room

• Mentor engineers on search and backend practices

What You Have:

• 6+ years of professional software engineering, much of it building and running backend systems in production

• Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology or related field

• Search engines, in depth (3+ years hands-on with Elasticsearch, Solr, or OpenSearch): mappings and analyzers, Query DSL, relevance tuning, aggregations, cluster sizing and operations, reindexing strategies. You've owned a cluster, not just queried one.

• Python: strong, idiomatic Python 3 (typing, async, packaging, pytest) and at least one web framework such as Flask or FastAPI
